stem: Which component sends notifications to email, Slack or PagerDuty?

options.text: Alertmanager
options.note: Right. Alertmanager receives alerts from Prometheus and turns them into notifications.

options.text: The Prometheus server
options.note: The server evaluates alerting rules and sends alerts to Alertmanager. It doesn't send notifications itself.

options.text: The Pushgateway
options.note: The Pushgateway holds metrics pushed by batch jobs. It has nothing to do with notifications.

options.text: An exporter
options.note: Exporters expose metrics from third-party systems. They don't handle alerts.

explanation: Prometheus fires alerts, and Alertmanager groups, de-duplicates, silences and routes them as notifications to receivers such as email, PagerDuty or Slack.
hint: The server raises the alarm, but someone else makes the phone call.

stem: What is the Pushgateway mainly for?

options.text: Letting short-lived batch jobs make their metrics available after they exit
options.note: Right. A batch job may finish before Prometheus ever scrapes it, so it pushes its final metrics to the Pushgateway, and Prometheus scrapes them from there.

options.text: Turning Prometheus into a push-based system for all services
options.note: The docs recommend it only for specific cases. Normal collection is pull-based.

options.text: Forwarding alerts to Alertmanager
options.note: The Prometheus server sends alerts to Alertmanager directly.

options.text: Long-term storage of metrics
options.note: Long-term storage is done through remote write integrations, not the Pushgateway.

explanation: The overview describes the Pushgateway as supporting short-lived jobs, and the glossary says it persists the most recent push from batch jobs so Prometheus can scrape them after they terminate.
hint: Think about a job that runs for 10 seconds when the scrape interval is a minute.

stem: You need metrics from a database whose source code you can't change. What do you typically run?

options.text: An exporter next to the database that translates its stats into Prometheus format
options.note: Right. That's the job of an exporter: expose metrics for systems you can't instrument directly.

options.text: A client library added to the database's code
options.note: Client libraries are for code you own and can change. Here you can't change the code.

options.text: A second Prometheus server inside the database
options.note: Prometheus scrapes metrics. It doesn't extract them from a database's internals.

options.text: Alertmanager
options.note: Alertmanager handles alerts. It doesn't collect metrics.

explanation: An exporter runs alongside the application and exposes Prometheus metrics, usually by converting metrics from a non-Prometheus format.
hint: You can't edit the code, so instrumentation has to live outside it.

stem: Which of these does the Prometheus server itself do? Select all that apply.

options.text: Scrape metrics from targets
options.note: Right. The server pulls metrics from instrumented jobs.

options.text: Store samples in a local time series database
options.note: Right. Scraped samples are stored locally.

options.text: Evaluate recording and alerting rules
options.note: Right. The server runs rules to record new series or generate alerts.

options.text: De-duplicate and route notifications to receivers
options.note: That's Alertmanager's job, not the server's.

explanation: The architecture section says Prometheus scrapes metrics, stores all samples locally, and runs rules to record new time series or generate alerts. Notification handling belongs to Alertmanager.
hint: One of these happens after the alert has left the server.

stem: What does a recording rule do?

options.text: Precomputes a frequently used or expensive expression and saves the result as new time series
options.note: Right. This makes dashboards and alerts that use the expression cheaper and faster.

options.text: Records raw logs alongside metrics
options.note: Prometheus doesn't store logs. Recording rules produce time series.

options.text: Records which users ran which queries
options.note: That isn't what recording rules are. They're about precomputing query results.

options.text: Starts recording metrics from a new target
options.note: Targets come from scrape configuration and service discovery, not recording rules.

explanation: The glossary defines recording rules as precomputing frequently needed or computationally expensive expressions and saving their results as a new set of time series.
hint: The word "record" here means saving a result.

stem: Why is each Prometheus server designed to be standalone, without relying on network storage?

options.text: So monitoring keeps working when other parts of the infrastructure are broken
options.note: Right. The overview says Prometheus is meant to be the system you go to during an outage.

options.text: Because Prometheus can't write to disk
options.note: It does write to local disk, in its TSDB.

options.text: Because it stores everything only in memory
options.note: Data is persisted to disk in blocks, with a WAL protecting recent data.

options.text: Because standalone servers give 100% accurate data
options.note: The docs say Prometheus is not suited to cases that need 100% accuracy, such as billing.

explanation: Prometheus is designed for reliability. Each server is standalone, so you can rely on it during failures without extensive infrastructure.

stem: How does Prometheus's local storage protect the most recent samples, which are still in memory, against a crash?

options.text: With a write-ahead log (WAL) that is replayed on restart
options.note: Right. The in-memory head block is secured by the WAL.

options.text: By replicating each sample to a second server
options.note: Local storage isn't clustered or replicated.

options.text: By writing each sample to a separate file immediately
options.note: Samples are grouped into blocks. The WAL is what covers the in-memory part.

options.text: It doesn't. Recent data is always lost on a crash
options.note: The WAL exists precisely to replay recent data after a crash.

explanation: Samples are grouped into two-hour blocks. The current block is kept in memory and secured by a write-ahead log, which is replayed when the server restarts.
hint: Databases often keep a log of writes before applying them.

stem: Into what time windows does Prometheus initially group ingested samples on disk?

options.text: Two-hour blocks
options.note: Right. Ingested samples are grouped into two-hour blocks, which are later compacted into larger ones.

options.text: One-day blocks
options.note: Larger blocks only appear later, through compaction. The initial blocks cover two hours.

options.text: Five-minute blocks
options.note: Too small. The storage docs give two hours.

options.text: One block per metric name
options.note: Blocks are organised by time window, not by metric name.

explanation: The storage page says ingested samples are grouped into two-hour blocks. Compaction later merges them into longer blocks in the background.

stem: Local Prometheus storage isn't clustered or replicated. What feature lets you send samples to a separate long-term storage system?

options.text: Remote write
options.note: Right. Remote write sends ingested samples on the fly to other systems, such as long-term storage.

options.text: The Pushgateway
options.note: The Pushgateway receives pushed metrics for scraping. It isn't for long-term storage.

options.text: Recording rules
options.note: Recording rules create new series inside Prometheus. They don't ship data elsewhere.

options.text: Alertmanager
options.note: Alertmanager handles alerts, not samples.

explanation: Remote write sends ingested samples to other systems, and remote read lets queries transparently read from them. This is how Prometheus gains durable or long-term storage.
hint: The name describes writing somewhere remote.

stem: How does Grafana typically get data from Prometheus?

options.text: It sends PromQL queries to the Prometheus server's API
options.note: Right. Grafana is an API consumer that queries Prometheus with PromQL.

options.text: It scrapes the applications' /metrics endpoints itself
options.note: Prometheus does the scraping. Grafana queries Prometheus.

options.text: It reads the TSDB block files directly from disk
options.note: Grafana uses the HTTP API rather than reading the server's files.

options.text: Prometheus pushes every sample to Grafana as it arrives
options.note: Grafana pulls data by querying when it draws a dashboard.

explanation: The overview notes that Grafana or other API consumers can be used to visualise collected data. They query it using PromQL.
hint: Grafana is described as an API consumer.
